extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics faculty, department administrators, and assessment coordinators designing or implementing quantitative literacy (QR) programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, implementing, and assessing a college-level Quantitative Reasoning/Quantitative Literacy (QR) program, including learning objectives, course design, placement, assessment methods, scoring rubrics, and department participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct logical arguments and quantitative problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to construct a logical argument based on rules of inference and to develop strategies for solving quantitative problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should learn to form logically consistent arguments and to devise strategies for approaching and solving quantitative problems (explicitly listed as a core learning goal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret mathematical models and draw inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret mathematical models such as formulas, graphs, tables, and schematics, and draw inferences from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction and assessment should require students to read models in multiple representations and extract meaningful conclusions for real situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent mathematical information in multiple forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent mathematical information symbolically, visually, numerically, and verbally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must be able to convert between symbolic, graphical, numerical and written descriptions and use each representation appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sense of everyday numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to make sense of numbers that a person encounters in the real world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A QR program should emphasize practical number sense and contextual interpretation of numeric claims encountered outside the classroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret statistical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to interpret statistical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be trained to read, critique, and draw valid conclusions from statistical summaries, tables, and studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand basic probability in real-world contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to develop an understanding of basic probability relative to real world situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course content and assessments should include basic probability concepts framed in applied, real-world scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use arithmetic, algebraic, geometric and statistical methods to solve problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Use arithmetical, algebraic, geometric and statistical methods to solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect students to apply an appropriate toolbox (arithmetic through statistics) to model and solve contextual problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate and check answers for reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and check answers to mathematical problems in order to determine reasonableness, identify alternatives, and select optimal results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should include tasks where students must produce estimates, perform reasonableness checks, consider alternatives, and justify selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciate role of mathematics in real-world domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciate the role of mathematics in the real world, in particular, the use of mathematics in politics and business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program goals should foster awareness of mathematics’ applications and relevance in varied societal and professional contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits of mathematical and statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that mathematical and statistical methods have limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be taught to identify assumptions, limitations, and domains of applicability of quantitative methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the importance of department-learned skills for future QR courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the importance of mathematical skills learned in the mathematics department in future QR courses in their own field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program should explicitly link department coursework to downstream QR courses in other departments and communicate those connections to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand uses and limitations of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the uses and limitations of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should include appropriate use of calculators/computational tools and critique of their limits; technology is not a substitute for conceptual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAT103 QR course content specification
rubrics_metrics.description: MAT103: Quantitative Reasoning is a survey QR course covering logic and problem solving; number sense and estimation; statistical interpretation and basic probability; interpreting mathematical models; and further applications to the use of mathematics in politics and business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core QR survey course should include these topical components and serve a broad fraction of students (explicitly MAT103 is designed to serve at least 40% of MMC students).

rubrics_metrics.name: Course-level placement and credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Course designations and credit/placement rules: MAT052 is a 1-credit basic math skills course (elective, pass/fail) and does not satisfy MMC's QR requirements; other courses (MAT101, MAT103, MAT105, MAT111 etc.) are structured to meet QR needs depending on placement and major.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program must specify which courses satisfy QR, which are remedial, pass/fail policy, and how students progress (placement tests determine enrollment paths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student self-assessment 0–3 scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Students self-assess their knowledge level relative to course content using a 0–3 numerical scale where 3 = Exceptional, 2 = Expected, 1 = Improved, 0 = Inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students place a numerical value for each listed skill, bring the grid to advising, and advisors provide feedback; self-assessment is used alongside instructor assessment to guide placement and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation workflow for low self-assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student's knowledge of a particular content area is 0 or 1, a worksheet on that content area will be provided to increase the knowledge level to at least 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program must include targeted remedial materials and a process to raise students to expected competency before enrolling in QR courses in their department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-placement testing with performance expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give students in MAT052 and MAT101 pre- and post-math placement tests. The expectation is that students will score at least 70% on the math competency exam upon finishing MAT101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre/post testing to measure skill gains; set clear performance targets (e.g., 70% threshold) for success in specific courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio evidence and reflective assessment in MAT103
rubrics_metrics.description: For MAT103, students will collect homework problems, projects, or exam problems demonstrating fulfillment of learning goals; students will reflect on these problems and these artifacts will count as an exam grade toward the final course grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collected student work plus reflective writing as direct evidence of meeting learning objectives and as part of course grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental participation and communication responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating departments must identify course(s) in their department as QR courses; identify math skills used in those courses that are covered in prerequisite math courses; give students a skill list when they declare a major and before enrolling in math courses; and collect/monitor data on student success relative to those skills annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-disciplinary coordination is required: departments must commit to identifying QR offerings, align prerequisites, communicate expectations to students, and share assessment data with the mathematics department.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDSU three general assessment capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment focuses on three general capabilities: (1) Analyzing and interpreting data and reasoning to reach sound decisions; (2) Using mathematical concepts in real-world settings to model, develop strategies, and interpret outcomes meaningfully; (3) Critical and logical thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment instruments should be designed to measure these three overarching capabilities rather than a single core list of skills for all students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor-defined test target categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests should measure (a) prerequisite skills essential for success in the course, (b) skills that instructors expect students to have on entry to the course, (c) knowledge that will not be covered in the course except for possible quick review, and (d) knowledge demonstrating readiness to comprehend real-world mathematical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests are custom-designed with heavy instructor involvement to target these four categories so results are actionable for course instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic A–E scoring rubric for items
rubrics_metrics.description: Every problem is rated holistically A–E: A = completely correct; B = basically correct with a minor error; C = flawed response but quite close to correct; D = some appropriate action but far short of a solution; E = no response or nothing relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use holistic A–E ratings for scoring free-response assessment items and report distributions (percentages) of students in each grade band to indicate levels of mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing logistics and reporting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests are given early in the semester, scored by mathematics graduate students, and returned to students within a week or two; results are summarized in reports for instructors including achievement, backgrounds, and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment programs should minimize extra demands on participants, return results promptly to inform instruction, and produce reports that support instructor and departmental decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of example problems and success-rate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Include example test items with annotated success rates (percent of students receiving A/B etc.) to illustrate typical performance and to inform curriculum/assessment decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting of item-level success rates helps reveal unexpected student difficulties and informs where curricular adjustments or targeted instruction are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade thresholds for QR-related majors
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-specified grade requirements: Business administration, accounting, and marketing majors are required to successfully complete (grade C or better) MAT111; business/professional communication majors must successfully complete (grade C or better) MAT105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set explicit minimum grade standards in prerequisite math courses as part of QR program policy for particular majors.
